card: Plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-accelerated SHA256 compression routine into libsecp256k1 contexts. It restructures ECC context lifecycle management to decouple it from key primitives and introduces a dedicated verification context that replaces libsecp256k1's static context. Benchmarks on ARM64 demonstrate a 13% speedup in ECDSA signing and a 7% speedup in Schnorr signing, while verification performance remains essentially flat. No prerequisites or follow-up dependencies are noted.
changed_since_previous: Minor rebase fixups and test updates with no change to the core approach or commit structure.
evidence: Author ARM64 arm_shani benchmarks report signing latency reductions of 13% for ECDSASign (79.2 µs down to 69.3 µs) and 7% for SchnorrSign (39.9 µs down to 37.1 µs), with verification latency essentially unchanged (-0% to -1%).
problem: libsecp256k1 defaults to an internal software SHA256 implementation, leaving CPU hardware crypto extensions unused during signing and internal hashing. Furthermore, libsecp256k1's static context cannot be configured with custom callbacks, forcing a restructuring of ECC context initialization to support hardware acceleration on public operations.

risk.why: A flaw in the SHA256 compression hook or context lifecycle handling during signature verification or generation could cause consensus splits or produce invalid signatures.

scope_notes: Includes a scripted-diff commit replacing secp256k1_context_static with GetSecp256k1PublicContext() throughout src/pubkey.cpp.
summary: Plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-optimized SHA256 compression function (using SHA-NI, ARMv8, or SSE4) into libsecp256k1 signing and verification contexts. It refactors ECC context lifecycle management out of key.h into ecc_context and common/ecc_init, and introduces a dedicated public verification context to replace secp256k1_context_static across pubkey operations.
